newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 11.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Prime Minister Jim Bolger last night predicted ACT NZ leader Richard Prebble would win the Wellington Central seat, in a shock change of strategy aimed at saving National's chances of governing. Victory for ACT in the seat could hold the key to the make-up of the next government, because winning an electorate seat would mean ACT would not have to breach the five percent threshold. Page 1.
National's Wellington Central candidate Mark Thomas asked Prime Minister Jim Bolger's office for a public endorsement just hours before Bolger predicted that ACT NZ would win the seat. Page 1.
New Zealand First is asking its candidates to sign over five percent of their salaries if they become MPs, to help pay for its election campaign. Page 2.

A coalition of Labour-Alliance-New Zealand First is favoured by voters as the best option for a government, according to an NBR-Consultus poll published today. But the grouping will not happen, with the Alliance ruling out entering any coalitions not negotiated before tomorrow's election. Page 2.

Despite trading marginally below budget in the first quarter, fertiliser and drug maker Fernz Corporation is confident of achieving a nine percent lift in net profit to $47.3 million for the year to May 1997. Page 21.

Investor complacency in the sharemarket has been replaced with pre-election nerves as the benchmark NZSE 40 index closed down yesterday for the third day running, marked by profit taking in Telecom. Page 21.

New Zealanders' non-housing savings have been rising more than eight percent annually, according to the Westpac Financial Services FPG household savings indicator. The indicator shows savings - not counting housing - rising an annual 8.7 percent in the March quarter and 8.8 percent in the June quarter. Page 21.
The second DHL export indicator survey shows New Zealand exporters are more optimistic about export orders over the next five years than over the next 12 months. Page 21.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Labour has edged still closer to National in the final week of the election campaign, but none of the probable coalition partnerships seem likely to emerge with a clear majority when the votes are counted. National still leads with 33 percent support, according to the New Zealand Herald-Waikato University election poll. Labour has added nearly two points to 29.4
percent of committed voters in the poll, completed on Wednesday night.
National's desperation before the cruel logic of MMP led Prime Minister Jim Bolger last night to hint that National voters support ACT NZ Richard Prebble in Wellington Central.
Prime Minister Jim Bolger has pulled out of a head-to-head radio debate with Labour leader Helen Clark after National radio abruptly changed the format to include other leaders.

Former Prime Minister David Lange wants Labour to form a minority government which does not initially include either New Zealand First or the Alliance as coalition partners. Lange suggested the parties spend six months working out what their bottom lines were before forming a "coherent" coalition.

Party leaders played out a last-minute positioning game as the election campaign wound down yesterday. In Waikato, Prime Minister Jim Bolger accused Labour leader Helen Clark of "returning to her socialist roots" by courting the Alliance. Meanwhile, in Wellington Clark was trying to apply pressure on
Jim Anderton by questioning if the Alliance would support a Labour-led government.
Fernz Corporation yesterday became the second top 10 company to adopt minority veto take-over restriction.

Mercury Energy has again raised the stakes in its bidding war for strategic positions in Power New Zealand. Mercury said yesterday it had lifted the offered price range for the shares held by WEL Energy and six district councils to NZ$10-15, from NZ$7.25-$10.

Institutions picked up the lion's share of the volume in Wilson and Horton yesterday on the first day of a market stand by Dublin-based Independent Newspapers. Of the 861,633 shares traded, only 186,725 went to Independent Newspapers, which is bidding $11 a share.
